D01.en: A colossal gilded imperial statue of a perfect, untouchable Tang emperor standing on a lotus pedestal inside a vast ceremonial hall, face serene and idealized, golden light, incense haze, worshippers reduced to tiny blurred silhouettes below, the icon of an unchallengeable ruler

D02.en: A crude popular woodblock-printed book page and a gaudy opera stage shown together: a painted fan backdrop of a righteous son defying a wicked father, a costumed actor in exaggerated gesture, cheap bright lantern light, deliberately kitsch and simplistic, the reduction of history to a moral fable

D03.en: A frontier battlefield at dawn crowded with hard-bitten Tang generals on tired horses in mismatched armour, a hundred weathered faces rather than one hero, dust and stripped standard poles, the frontier won by an entire army not a lone man

D04.en: An ancient Chinese aristocratic family genealogy scroll spread on a dark table, three imperial clan names linked by red-ink marriage lines to a single powerful father's name, branching connections to three reigning houses, the web of a military aristocracy, lamplight

D05.en: Early Tang Chang'an at first light seen from a high wall: a capital just taken, new banners on fresh timber, smoke still rising from repaired walls, carts of grain entering the gate, cautious exhausted soldiers, a dynasty settling in

D06.en: A capable Tang crown prince in formal crimson court robes standing in a lit council chamber, one hand resting on a map of Hebei, sharp attentive eyes, documents neatly organised before him, unmistakably competent and in command, not a buffoon

D07.en: The Prince of Qin in dark lamellar armour on a dais before a war council, a command baton in hand, helmeted officers kneeling in rows below him, the banner of his own command behind, absolute authority over the field army

D08.en: Two halves of one war machine shown in cross-section: on one side disciplined infantry and armourers at a foundry, on the other a vast frontier cavalry line, both halves of a single state's division of labour, a clean schematic of a working partnership

D09.en: A battlefield dominated by a single man's standard at its centre, endless ranks of Tang cavalry receding to the horizon all flying the same banner, the scale of one commander's accumulated victory, dust and low sun

D10.en: A parallel administration growing inside a palace: a shadowed side hall lit by lamplight where a prince's own clerks work their own registers, seals and appointment writs stacked on their own desks, a second government forming within the state

D11.en: A Tang general mounting a carriage to leave the capital, a posting order in his hand, the city gate behind him and a heavy gold chest half-hidden under a cloak in a shadowed alcove beside it, two fates being quietly arranged

D12.en: A calm, chilling advisory scene: two officials in plain dark robes studying a map across a low table in an Eastern Palace library, scrolls fanned out, one pointing precisely at a border, the patience of a strategy that never raises its voice

D13.en: Turkic steppe horsemen crossing a frontier river at dusk, thousands of fur-hooded riders, wolf-head standards, torchlight on the far bank, the smoke of burned frontier watchtowers, an invasion season opening again

D14.en: An emptied war camp at night: bare horse lines with only a few riders left, trampled ground, abandoned equipment, and in the foreground a lone man standing where his army used to be, a trap closing, dusk

D15.en: The night outside a prince's mansion in a capital: watchers in dark lanes behind walls, a lantern deliberately shielded, a patrolling guard turning a corner, the silent net drawn tight around a household

D16.en: A clan banquet in a warm lamplit hall, an ornate wine cup raised, a young general's face tightening as he drinks, a nearby courtier watching him too closely, the corner of a rumour taking shape over poisoned wine

D17.en: A heavy sealed codex of ancestral law resting on an altar between two throne chairs, one chair draped in mourning cloth, the other abandoned, the price of defying the founding order made physical, cold light

D18.en: A young man in battered armour refusing to go down, a wolf's dark eyes held in the frame above him, blood on his brow, absolute defiance that is neither saintly nor lamb-like, hard cold light

D19.en: A reader confronting a heavy open volume at a desk, one hand pressed flat on the page, lamplight raking across dense columns, a puzzled furrowed brow, the moment a question forms

D20.en: A court official standing alone in a vast hall while other seats remain occupied but turned away, courtiers looking down, his own allies conspicuously absent, political isolation made spatial

D21.en: Looking down into a deep well of overlapping connections: a lattice of knotted cords and hidden lineages lit from below, an ancient military aristocracy's real structure, unseen and unbreakable

D22.en: Two clasped hands in near darkness, no document and no seal anywhere in frame, an understanding sealed by grip alone, candlelight catching only the hands, politics where paper is unnecessary

D23.en: A war-band of Tang commanders in a lamplit tent, three senior men at the centre with the bearing of long service, armoured officers standing behind them, the hard core of an ancient military aristocracy, firelight on armour

D24.en: A row of weathered Tang generals in faded armour weighing two empty throne chairs set side by side, one chair with fresh cushions, one bare, the calculating silence of soldiers deciding whose rise will keep their estates

D25.en: The north gate of a Tang palace seen head-on at night, massive vermilion timber and iron fittings, the narrow killing ground between the emperor's bedchamber and the imperial guard camp, a few lamplight pools, the shortest fatal corridor in history

D26.en: A weathered stone epitaph tablet, its carved Chinese characters catching raking lamplight, a scholar's gloved hand steadying it, dust in the air, a discovery that a modern century unearthed, a cold museum-like intimacy

D27.en: A veteran gate guard of the Eastern Palace standing at his post on a palace threshold at dusk, disciplined and utterly trustworthy in appearance, a heavy iron ring of keys at his belt, the most reliable man in the empire

D28.en: Two plain-robed men slipping through a shadowed side entrance of a walled residence at night, one carrying a sealed document, a guard turning away up the wall, a secret summons delivered

D29.en: A lamplit inner tent before dawn: a prince bent over a low desk drafting on silk, brush moving carefully, two commanders behind him with hands resting on sheathed sabres, the conspirators at work while the city sleeps

D30.en: A tall tower of stacked game pieces on a lacquered board, one side toppled and scattered, a single hand still resting on the last standing piece, no second player in frame, an all-or-nothing wager

D31.en: Horse hooves on wet flagstones at dawn, two riders approaching along a palace wall from a side gate, horses alert and ears forward, guards watching from a parapet above, the final approach
